### Project Tutorial: Build a Large Language Model from Scratch in Python
**Category:** ai-machine-learning | **Language:** Python | **Difficulty:** Advanced
**Summary:** Construct a complete GPT-like transformer language model from first principles: BPE tokenization, multi-head self-attention, layer normalization, residual connections, and autoregressive text generation.
**What You Will Build:** A PyTorch-based autoregressive transformer model capable of tokenizing text corpora, training on raw literature, calculating causal masked attention, and generating coherent text completions word-by-word.
**Source URL:** https://github.com/rasbt/LLMs-from-scratch
**GitHub:** https://github.com/rasbt/LLMs-from-scratch
**Learning Outcomes:** Implement Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) vocabulary tokenization, Build causal scaled dot-product attention with future token masking, Implement multi-head attention blocks with learned projection matrices, Apply pre-layer normalization (LayerNorm) and GELU feedforward layers, Implement autoregressive generation with top-k and temperature sampling

**Steps:**
- Step 1: Text Tokenization & Positional Embeddings
- Step 2: Causal Scaled Dot-Product Self-Attention
- Step 3: Multi-Head Attention & Transformer Block
- Step 4: Autoregressive Text Generation & Sampling

metadata.title: Build a Large Language Model from Scratch in Python

### Project Tutorial: Build Your Own Container Using Less Than 100 Lines of Go
**Category:** developer-tools | **Language:** Go | **Difficulty:** Advanced
**Summary:** Understand Linux containerization from first principles by creating an isolated process runtime using Linux namespaces, cgroups, chroot, and syscalls in Go.
**What You Will Build:** A container engine CLI (`docker run cmd`) that isolates processes with their own hostname, process tree (PID 1), filesystem root, and memory limits using native Linux kernel primitives.
**Source URL:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8fi7uSYlOdc
**GitHub:** 
**Learning Outcomes:** Understand what Linux namespaces actually do (UTS, PID, Mount, Network), Re-exec Go processes to achieve PID 1 isolation inside child containers, Isolate filesystems using chroot and mount private procfs filesystems, Restrict memory and CPU consumption using Linux cgroups, Secure container environments against privilege escalation

**Steps:**
- Step 1: Fork and Execute Arbitrary Commands
- Step 2: Isolate Hostname with UTS Namespace
- Step 3: Isolate Process Tree with PID Namespace
- Step 4: Filesystem Sandboxing with chroot & Mounts
- Step 5: Resource Restrictions with cgroups v2

**Summary:** Build your own Front-end Framework / Library using JavaScript
**What You Will Build:** A 400-line front-end library (`Didact`) that replicates React 18: converts JSX to virtual DOM, breaks rendering work into incremental fiber units with requestIdleCallback, performs DOM diffing, and manages reactive component state.
**Source URL:** https://pomb.us/build-your-own-react/

### Project Tutorial: Build Your Own SQLite Database from Scratch
**Category:** databases | **Language:** C | **Difficulty:** Intermediate
**Summary:** Build a lightweight relational database inspired by SQLite, featuring a REPL front-end, bytecode compiler, in-memory paging, and B-Tree disk persistence.
**What You Will Build:** A functional relational database that accepts SQL queries (`INSERT`, `SELECT`), parses statements into internal bytecode instructions, stores records inside fixed-size 4KB memory pages, and persists tables to disk using a B-Tree structure.
**Source URL:** https://cstack.github.io/db_tutorial/
**GitHub:** https://github.com/cstack/db_tutorial
**Learning Outcomes:** Understand how SQL query text is transformed into executable bytecode, Implement memory-paged storage architecture with 4096-byte blocks, Build a B-Tree node layout supporting root splits and logarithmic searching, Safely persist and restore records to and from disk, Design an interactive REPL with custom meta-commands (.exit, .constants, .btree)

**Steps:**
- Step 1: Design the Interactive REPL & Input Buffer
- Step 2: Implement the SQL Tokenizer & Prepared Statement Parser
- Step 3: Define the Row Layout & In-Memory Pager
- Step 4: Disk Persistence & Flushing with Paged I/O
- Step 5: B-Tree Node Architecture & Leaf Node Layout

### Project Tutorial: Write Yourself a Git! (Content-Addressable Storage)
**Category:** developer-tools | **Language:** Python | **Difficulty:** Beginner
**Summary:** Build a complete Git client from scratch in Python, implementing content-addressable storage, blob/tree/commit objects, zlib compression, and repository staging.
**What You Will Build:** A custom command-line program (`wyag` or `mygit`) capable of initializing a `.git` directory, hashing files into blobs, organizing directory trees, generating commit objects, and checking out branches.
**Source URL:** https://wyag.thb.lt/
**GitHub:** 
**Learning Outcomes:** Understand the internal file structure of the `.git` directory, Implement the 4 fundamental Git object types: blob, tree, commit, tag, Compress and decompress objects using zlib with SHA-1 addressing, Parse and construct binary tree objects representing directories, Traverse commit parent chains to inspect repository history

**Steps:**
- Step 1: Initialize the .git Directory Hierarchy
- Step 2: The Object Database & Blob Storage
- Step 3: Read Objects with 'cat-file'
- Step 4: Tree Objects (Directories & Permissions)
- Step 5: Commit Objects & Commit History Traversal
